c-01-c3.text: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14 (2011). N1570: Committee Draft ISO/IEC 9899:201x, Programming languages: C (6.5.2.1 Array subscripting). WG14 C11 committee draft (HTML mirror at port70.net).
c-01-c3.quote: The definition of the subscript operator [] is that E1[E2] is identical to (*((E1)+(E2))).
c-01-c3.claim: arr[i] is exactly equivalent to *(arr + i)

c-01-c3.text: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14 (2011). N1570: Committee Draft ISO/IEC 9899:201x, Programming languages: C (6.5.6 Additive operators). WG14 C11 committee draft (HTML mirror at port70.net).
c-01-c3.quote: the result is the difference of the subscripts of the two array elements.
c-01-c3.claim: p2 - p1 returns the number of elements between them, not bytes.

c-01-c3.text: MITRE Corporation (2024). CWE-121: Stack-based Buffer Overflow. Common Weakness Enumeration, MITRE.
c-01-c3.quote: The most prominent is the stored return address, the memory address at which execution should continue once the current function is finished executing.
c-01-c3.claim: Buffer overflows are precisely this: writing past the end of an array, often onto the stack where return addresses live.

c-01-c2.text: MITRE Corporation (2024). CWE-415: Double Free. Common Weakness Enumeration, MITRE.
c-01-c2.quote: When a program calls free() twice with the same argument, the program's memory management data structures may become corrupted, potentially leading to the reading or modification of unexpected memory addresses.
c-01-c2.claim: Free twice and you get double-free corruption.
